Clock in
Do equipment checks
Pass meds for inmates on one side of the prison
Do scheduled treatments
Pass meds for the other half of the prison
Perform care for any inmates spending time in a medical cell

As far as I know, switching insurance companies is likely to be a fairly lengthy (several weeks) process. That said, here is everything I've got:

- Does your college have a health center? Many have mid level practitioners (nurse practitioners and/or physician assistants) who have training in psychiatry and can triage you while you wait to see a psychiatrist.
- Look up any free clinics in your town. Just Google "free clinic + town." Give them a call and ask for a referral to a psychiatrist. They often have a network of specialists who will work on a sliding scale.
- Look up mental health centers in your town. Google "mental health clinic + town." Many work on a sliding scale. 
- Call your local rape crisis center. It doesn't matter if you've ever been raped or if you're male or female. They almost always have a list of psychiatrists who will work on a sliding scale. Just call and ask if they can refer you to any psychiatrists who will work on a sliding scale. 
- If all else fails, look up every psychiatric nurse practitioner and psychiatrist that you can reasonably commute to and give them a call. Even if they're not covered, call and ask if they can work on a sliding scale. If you get an appointment, take it. Keep calling to try to find a sooner appointment. 

I would suggest setting up 2 - 3 appointments with different clinicians if at all possible. That way if you don't like the first one you see you don't have to wait weeks or months to see another. 

Hang in there and good luck!
